quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid getting tired on a long motorcycle ride?
questions.explanation: To stay alert on long rides, limit your riding time each day and take rest breaks. Do not use stimulants because you will feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for it to start moving.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, move to a different lane to give it space. Slow down and be ready to stop when you pass the emergency scene.

questions.question: When does a motorcycle have less grip for braking?

options.text: When the motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans during a turn, there is less grip available for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must do it carefully.

questions.question: What helps other drivers see your motorcycle best during normal riding?

options.text: Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on day and night to help others see you. Use your high beam whenever it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Help you blend in with traffic.
Give you a way to escape danger.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a way to escape danger.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should keep you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It should also keep other drivers out of your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When traffic is slow or stopped, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
Weave in and out of traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between rows of stopped or slow vehicles is dangerous. Cars may change lanes, open doors, or have arms out the window. Motorcycles need a full lane to ride safely.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may cause poor traction.
questions.explanation: Poor traction can happen on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel roads; lane markings; and metal plates or utility hole covers.

questions.question: Which lane position best stops other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The right side of the lane

questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane discourages other drivers from trying to fit into your space. When following a car, riding in the center helps the driver see you in their mirror.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should your feet be?
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not point your toes downward, as they may get caught between the road and the footrests.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast a small vehicle like a motorcycle is moving or how far away it is. Do not assume that other drivers can accurately see your speed and location.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect a rider's ability to operate a motorcycle safely?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to safely ride a motorcycle. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop line before moving forward to improve their view of cross traffic.
Ignore the stop line and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop line then proceed through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line before moving forward to improve their view of cross traffic.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection with a stop line or stop sign, stop first where indicated. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward to look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: Where do most motorcycle and car accidents happen?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle and car accidents happen at intersections. Usually, the car driver fails to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet on a moving motorcycle?
questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or motorized bicycle.

questions.question: When being passed on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed on the left, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the right side is dangerous because it may cause the passing driver to return to your lane too quickly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers to follow specific traffic laws. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When riding near a truck:

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
You should concentrate on operating your motorcycle and not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Avoid the blind spots of large trucks. Remember: if you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the truck driver cannot see you.

questions.question: If you approach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to signal that the other vehicle should proceed.
You should continue through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, if you arrive at the same time as another driver, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull to the side of the road until the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the oily center stripe of the lane becomes very slippery and dangerous. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is usually safest, but this can vary.

questions.question: A person is considered intoxicated with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____ or higher.
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a person with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is considered intoxicated. You cannot drive if you are intoxicated.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue while driving, you should:
questions.explanation: Taking frequent rest breaks helps reduce fatigue on long trips. Caffeine may give you a quick boost, but you can crash when it wears off, making you even more tired.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when it takes longer to stop, when you can't see clearly, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: To shift to a higher gear, you must:

options.text: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift.
Place your foot over the shift lever and push.
Use your thumb to move the lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift.
questions.explanation: To shift to a higher gear, put your foot under the shift lever and lift it up.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the following distance should:
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to stop.
